recipes.name: Restaurant-Style Zuppa Toscana
ingredients_raw: 2 cups kale - washed, dried, and shredded

steps.text: Preheat the oven to 300 degrees F (150 degrees C).
Place sausage links onto a sheet pan and bake for 25 minutes, or until done. Cut links in half lengthwise, then cut at an angle into 1/2-inch slices.
Place bacon and onion in a large saucepan and cook over medium heat until onion is almost clear. Remove bacon and crumble. Set aside.
Add garlic into the pan with onion and cook together, about 1 minute. Add water, chicken soup base, and potatoes, simmer 15 minutes.
Add crumbled bacon, sausage, kale, and cream. Simmer, about 5 minutes, and serve.

raw_recipe.headline: Restaurant-Style Zuppa Toscana
raw_recipe.description: Restaurant-style soup. Crumbled bacon, Italian sausage, chopped kale, and cream are combined in this chicken stock based soup with potatoes.

review.reviewBody:
As a retired test kitchen chef, I am bound to dabble. So after reading all the reviews, I set to work to make a lower fat version and still maintain taste. I had researched the Top Secret version and felt I could even drop fat content on that one too.

1. I used hot italian turkey sausage. Yes it came in links, but I squeezed out the meat and cooked it. Then roll in paper towels to get out any remaining fat. 

2. Bacon and Onion should be cooked separately, then blended in at the last minute to meld flavors.
3. I dropped the water content, got rid of the cream and used entirely fat free half and half from the dairy section. Brilliant stuff and works well in this recipe. Smooth, rich, not too thin consistency

4. Some brave souls prefer to add pepper at this point, but I say "to taste"

5. I prefer the texture of Youkon Gold potatoes, but any young new potato with the skins on is great. If you like earthy, you can use russets. I have never been a fan of dirt so I stick with thin skins.

So play, enjoy! And don't forget the Romano!

This is a family favorite for us and I've made many times. I've switched up the style of sausage (kids like kielbasa, ground Italian is best), and the style of potatoes (sweet potatoes not so good), sometimes no bacon, spinach is better than bitter kale, fat free half n half works great to make it creamy, increase water and garlic, 2 carmelized onions. I don't follow all the complicated steps (it just takes too long!) but simplify.

My husband and I loved this recipe. After making this recipe I would change a few things. As one person suggested...yes, cook the bacon and onion separately. The bacon doesn't crisp up when cooking with the onion. Cook the bacon and use the drippings to cook the onion in. I used 2 1/2 quarts of water and 1/2 cup of cream. I used 3 small russet potatoes but I would have added one or two more. I used 3 chicken sausages from Sprouts. It was delicious!!!
It's OK, but it's not Toscana. Replace the smoked sausage links with ground spicy Italian sausage and you'll be much closer to that Toscana flavor.

Completely amazing, this soup! I used lean turkey sausage and fat free half-and half, adding a little corn starch for thickening. I cooked the kale longer because it was a bit tough, and made more of the broth/soup without adding extra sausage or bacon. It was absolutely marvelous! I want to eat it every day!

Awesome! I made this vegetarian by eliminating the bacon/sausage and adding more kale/onions. Also used 2 1/2 cans (14 oz) veggie broth instead of water/soup base. Also included crushed red pepper as recommended by other users. Very delicious, hearty soup.
This is a great soup! I went to make a second batch but the cream went bad, so I substituted a can on Cream Of Mushroom. Fantastic!!!

The only thing I will change the next time is the potatoes. I will cube them not slicing as they cooked up in a shorter amount of time. Other than that it was really great. It will be made here again!

I chose to make this 'copycat' soup as it is my husband's favorite at the restaurant that makes it. The recipe looked good but I tend to tweak soups for our own personal tastes. I used our own hot Italian sausages that dear hubby made. (Only four as hubby was liberal with the chile peppers!). Just removed the casings and cooked in some of the bacon fat with the onions, veggies and then garlic. Used more onion and garlic and I also added some celery, carrots, and an extra potato for extra veggies, flavour and color. I added a generous couple of teaspoons of Italian seasoning and parsley flakes. I used 6 cups of broth and at least a 1/2 cup of coffee cream. I also added extra chicken boulion to taste. I added the chopped kale towards the end and then the cream. This soup smelled heavenly as it simmered and had everyone drooling by the time supper was served. The soup met everyone's expectations and tasted great!!!

Awesome! If you told me it came from a famous italian restaurant chain I would have been none the wiser. Well worth the time to cook it. Only suggestion is I think about half the sausage would suffice. I like meat but that was a little over the top for the volume of soup you make. Extra kale is a plus too :). I can't even open the container without one of my dogs running up to me and sitting there in expectation of a taste of it

I followed the suggestions of others and fried the bacon by itself, drained the grease then sautéed the onion and garlic in the pan. In a large pot, I browned spicy hot Italian sausage, removed it from the pot and drained the grease. I added the chicken base/water to the pot with quartered potatoes and cooked for 20 minutes until the potatoes were tender then added all the other ingredients and cooked for an additional 10 minutes. Delish!
A1. Loved it. Used Italian sausage in place of the smoked.
Might be good as wrotten, but use ground Italian sausage if you want a true copycat! I am pretty sure Olive Garden does NOT have smoked sausage in their version.
Great soup. My husband loved it. I used chicken bullion (didn't have chicken stock base), crumbled sweet Italian sausage, and added mushrooms.
This is so delicious! My husband begs me to make it!!!

It’s a wonderful soup recipe. It’s a warm and flavorful recipe that’s easy to prepare. I added my personal touch and used a little Cajun seasoning. I forgot the bacon…adding it tomorrow 😂 It snowed and I made this❤️👍🏾

This is the second time I made the soup.. First time I made it exactly as the recipe called for except I used Sicilian hot sausage. This time I did the same except that I doubled the sausage, kale and heavy whipping cream because I wanted it to be hearty.. I removed the skins from the Sicilian hot sausage, broke it up and browned it in the pan. Added my onion and then garlic once it was almost cooked through and poured it all into pot with potatoes. It gives it an excellent flavor. Slightly spicy.. Yummy!

Awesome recipe; I used ground sweet Italian sausage instead; next time I’ll use low sodium chicken broth as the chicken base I used made it very salty; but the extra potatoes I added helped; used evaporated milk and some butter instead of whipping cream. My husband loved it and he’s

I've never had the soup from the "popular restaurant", but this soup is awesome! my family loved it. including my cat, whom I caught eating what little was left from my youngest child's bowl! 5/5 would recommend!
It was DELICIOUS! Only thing missing...the bread sticks. Will definitely make again.
